Body.Chest:
The chest’s task is to push the arms forward and away from the body. The chest is a very large and powerful muscle group consisting of three parts, the upper, the middle and the lower head. The parts ar naturally located in the same manner, the upper head is on the top and the lower head is on the bottom, whilst the middle head is smudged in between.
Exercises:
Bench pressDumbbell press
Incline bench press
Incline dumbbell press
Decline bench press
Decline dumbbell press
Pec deck
Dumbbell flies
Without equipment:
Normal pushups
Wide pushups

Body.Abs:
The abs are part of the core muscle group, and are a chain of muscles responsible for pulling the upper body towards the legs and vice versa, this plays a big part in stabilising the upper body and strengthening the core. The abs consists of the rectus abdominis which are the infamous six pack.
Exercises:
Russian twists
Cable crunches
Decline sit ups
Hanging leg raises
Without equipment:
Sit up
Crunches
Leg raises
Toe touches

Body.External obliques:
The Oblique muscles are also part of the core, and their main function is to pull the upper body sidewards towards the legs and vice versa, the obliques does a large part in stabilising the core as they are located on the sides of the core preventing the upper body from swaying from side to side, imagine the obliques as the wires on a radio tower, dragging on each side to hold the body upright.
Exercises:
Russian twists
Without equipment:
Toe touches
Side-crunches

Body.Shoulders:
The shoulder is the second largest arm muscle and is responsible for moving the shoulder joint, doing both push and pulling. The shoulder muscles are naturally located on the shoulders and consists of three parts, the anterior head on the front side, the lateral head in the middle or on the top if you will, and finally, the posterior head on the back side.
Exercises:
Dumbbell shoulder press (sitting/standing)
Barbell shoulder/overhead press (sitting/standing)
Lateral raises (dumbell/cable)
Reverse flies (machine/dumbbell/cable)
Front raises (dumbbell/plate)
Six ways (sitting/standing)
Without equipment:
Incline push-ups
Pike push-ups
Mountain climbers

Body.Biceps:
The biceps is the third largest arm muscle followed by the shoulder deltiod and the triceps. Its main task is to retract the arm, pulling the hand towards the shoulders. The bicep is, as its name states, built up of two parts, the long and the short head. The long head is located furthest out from the chest, whilst the short head is located on the inside of the arm, closest to the chest.
Exercises:
Bar curls / dumbbell curlsHammer curls (sitting/standing)
Preacher curls
Concentration curls
Chin ups
Without equipment:
Slow-fall-pushups

Body.Triceps:
The tricep is the largest arm muscle and is responsible for straightening out the elbow making the arm as long as possible. The tricep consists of three parts, the long head, the lateral head, and the medial head. The long head is located under the arm, the lateral head is most visible as it is located on the side of the arm, whilst the medial head is the hardest to see and is located closest to the elbow further out from the long head.
Exercises:
Tricep pushdowns
Skullcrushers
Dips
Without equipment:
Close-grip-pushups

Body.Forearms:
The forearms are a complex muscle group consisting of a whole list of heads. They allow for movement of the hands as well as the elbows, wrists and fingers. The forearm muscles are located between the elbow and the wrist.
Exercises:
Barbell wrist curls
Dumbbell wrist curls
Barbell reverse wrist curls
Dumbbell reverse wrist curls
Hand gripper squeezes
Plate pinch
Barbell rolls
Barbell reverse-grip rolls
Without equipment:
Forearm pushups
